posts.heading: September 26, 2026
posts.text:
Yesterday brought 282 feeder visits, slightly exceeding the recent weekly average of 278.7. The number of detected species dropped to 16, down from the previous seven-day average of 20.1, due to the absence of regulars such as the Mourning Dove and Ruby-throated Hummingbird, which had been recorded on every day of the prior week.

A second microphone began listening at 10:44, operating alongside the original unit. The Rose-breasted Grosbeak returned to the list after a seven-day absence, adding to the 16 species detected, while the Tufted Titmouse and Carolina Chickadee remained consistent presences.

Visual observations highlighted the Tufted Titmouse, which recorded the highest number of visits with 139, followed by the Carolina Chickadee with 63. A refill on the seed and nectar feeders the previous evening maintained the flow of regulars like the Northern Cardinal and House Finch. The day ended with a final visual of a Northern Cardinal.

posts.heading: September 25, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 266 visits and 22 species. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees remained the most frequent visitors, while Gray Catbird, Northern Flicker, and American Goldfinches were absent from the daily count.

Two feeders were refilled in the late afternoon, specifically the seed-feeder at 18:22 and the nectar-feeder at 18:38. House Finch and White-breasted Nuthatch were recorded daily for the past week.

A Northern Cardinal was visually confirmed 11 minutes before sunrise. By 19:03, a Blue Jay was observed 20 minutes before sunset.

posts.heading: September 24, 2026
posts.text:
The station recorded 360 feeder visits and 21 species, placing the day above the seven-day average for both visits and species count. Regular residents like the Northern Cardinal, Carolina Chickadee, and Tufted Titmouse remained consistent, holding their usual presence without significant shifts in their daily patterns.

The visitor list included several species recorded for the first time at this station, such as the Common Grackle and Red-breasted Nuthatch. The Eastern Kingbird also returned after eight days away, joining the usual mix of finches, wrens, and jays.

No changes to the station’s feeders or audio equipment were logged this week, so the shifts in numbers reflect natural variation in bird activity rather than new hardware or food sources.

posts.heading: September 23, 2026
posts.text:
The station recorded 321 feeder visits and 23 species, against a seven-day average of 235 visits and 20 species. Carolina Chickadees, Northern Cardinals, and Tufted Titmice dominated both audio detections and visual counts. Tufted Titmice accounted for 155 confirmed visits, while the Carolina Wren showed a significant spike in morning vocalizations.

The Gray Catbird marked its sixth appearance in the last week and the Black-and-white Warbler recorded its only visit during this period. The Red-shouldered Hawk and Pileated Woodpecker were also present, though less frequently. No new audio-only species were detected, and the core group of nine species recorded every day this week remained consistent with their recent history.

Activity spanned the full daylight period, beginning with a Gray Catbird sighting 4 minutes before sunrise and ending with a Ruby-throated Hummingbird 12 minutes before sunset. A Tufted Titmouse was observed perching on the rim of a treat bowl.

posts.heading: September 22, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 428 feeder visits, more than double the weekly average, while species counts stayed close to the typical range. Tufted Titmouse dominated the feeders with 203 visits, followed by House Finch and Northern Cardinal. Eastern Phoebe, a daily regular for the past week, was absent, while Cedar Waxwing returned after being away since September 15.

Brown-headed Cowbird, Cedar Waxwing, and Field Sparrow appeared for the first time at this station, with visual observations only and no corresponding first-time audio records. American Crow, Blue Jay, and Carolina Wren maintained their presence throughout the week.

Audio detections totaled 251, slightly below the seven-day average. Carolina Wren, Northern Cardinal, and Eastern Towhee remained the most frequent singers. No changes to feeders or audio sources occurred to account for the shift in numbers.

posts.heading: September 21, 2026
posts.text: The station recorded 124 feeder visits, compared to the recent weekly average of 230. The species count dipped to 18 from the mean of 20. Tufted Titmice were the most frequent visitors, seen 64 times, with Carolina Chickadees and Northern Cardinals following at 14 and 11 visits respectively. American Crows, Carolina Wrens, and Northern Cardinals provided the bulk of vocal detections. The day concluded with a Tufted Titmouse visiting 21 minutes before sunset, following its arrival 12 minutes before sunrise.
